userStories.title: seed_accounts.py — one-time bootstrap to populate accounts.json
userStories.description:
Current state: No accounts.json or seed_accounts.py exists at businesses/horizen-zkverify/scripts/. The directory contains zen_vfy_monitor_v1.py (a copy of v1 for reference) and .zen_vfy_seen.json.

What to build: Create businesses/horizen-zkverify/scripts/seed_accounts.py.

The script must:
1. Read TWITTER_BEARER_TOKEN from env (exit 1 with clear message if missing). Support --dry-run flag: prints what would be written, skips all API calls, exits 0.
2. Look up these 4 handles via GET https://api.twitter.com/2/users/by?usernames=HorizenOfficial,zkVerify_io,HorizenLabs,RolfVersluis with user.fields=description,id,name,username. If zkVerify_io returns 404/empty, print a warning and continue without it.
3. For each found seed account, fetch up to 100 accounts they follow via GET https://api.twitter.com/2/users/:id/following?max_results=100&user.fields=description,username,name. time.sleep(1) between each following request.
4. From following results, include accounts where bio (description) contains any of: ZEN, Horizen, zkVerify, VFY (case-insensitive). Tier = 'seed', note = 'followed by <seed_handle>'.
5. Write businesses/horizen-zkverify/scripts/accounts.json with schema: {"version": 1, "updated": "YYYY-MM-DD", "accounts": [{"id", "username", "name", "tier", "topics", "added", "note"}]}. topics = ['ZEN'] or ['VFY'] or ['ZEN','VFY'] based on bio content.
6. Print summary: N seed handles found, N following-based seeds added, total accounts written.

All file paths use Path(__file__).parent as base. Use urllib only (no requests). Python 3.9 compatible. Script is idempotent: overwrites accounts.json if it already exists.

userStories.title: accounts_state.py — helper module to track per-author appearance counts
userStories.description:
Current state: No accounts_state.py exists. This is a helper module that zen_vfy_monitor.py v2 will import.

What to build: Create businesses/horizen-zkverify/scripts/accounts_state.py.

Functions to implement:
  load_state(path: Path) -> dict  — loads accounts_state.json or returns {}
  save_state(state: dict, path: Path) -> None  — writes accounts_state.json
  record_appearance(state: dict, author_id: str, username: str, likes: int) -> dict  — increments appearances, adds likes, sets first_seen/last_seen (YYYY-MM-DD)
  get_promotable(state: dict, min_appearances: int = 3, min_likes: int = 3) -> list[dict]  — returns list of {id, username, appearances, total_likes} for accounts meeting both thresholds
  mark_noise(state: dict, author_id: str) -> dict  — sets noise=True on the state entry

Schema for each state entry:
  {username, appearances, total_likes, first_seen, last_seen, noise (optional bool)}

Python 3.9 compatible, stdlib only. No sibling imports in this file.

userStories.title: zen_vfy_monitor.py v2 — replace v1 with curated-account timeline monitor
userStories.description:
Current state: businesses/horizen-zkverify/scripts/zen_vfy_monitor_v1.py exists as v1 reference. We are writing the NEW v2 as businesses/horizen-zkverify/scripts/zen_vfy_monitor.py (this is a new file — zen_vfy_monitor_v1.py is the reference copy, do not modify it).

What to build: Create businesses/horizen-zkverify/scripts/zen_vfy_monitor.py as v2.

TOP OF FILE (before other imports):
  import sys
  from pathlib import Path
  sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))
  import accounts_state as acct_state

Carry forward from v1 (read zen_vfy_monitor_v1.py): QUERIES, SPAM_PATTERNS, POSITIVE_WORDS, NEGATIVE_WORDS, is_spam(), sentiment(), engagement_score(), load_seen(), save_seen(), send_email().

In send_email(), use full path for gog: /opt/homebrew/bin/gog (not just 'gog') so it works in cron on Jack's machine.

New v2 logic:

  STEP 1 — Timeline fetch for seed + tracked accounts:
    accounts_path = Path(__file__).parent / 'accounts.json'
    If accounts_path does not exist: skip Step 1, print warning.
    Load accounts. For each account where tier in ('seed', 'tracked'):
      Fetch original posts: GET /2/users/:id/tweets?max_results=10&start_time=48h_ago&tweet.fields=created_at,public_metrics,author_id&exclude=retweets
      Fetch all posts: GET /2/users/:id/tweets?max_results=10&start_time=48h_ago&tweet.fields=created_at,public_metrics,author_id (no exclude)
      time.sleep(0.5) between each request pair.
      Combine, deduplicate by tweet ID.
      Keep only tweets where text contains any of (case-insensitive): ZEN, $ZEN, Horizen, VFY, $VFY, zkVerify, zkverify.
      Attach 'tier' field to each kept tweet for badge rendering.

  STEP 2 — Cashtag search top-up + account promotion:
    Load accounts_state via acct_state.load_state(state_path).
    Run same two QUERIES as v1.
    For each tweet returned:
      If author_id already in accounts.json (any tier) → add tweet to pool with tier from accounts.json, skip state update.
      Else → acct_state.record_appearance(state, author_id, username, likes).
    After all search results: get_promotable = acct_state.get_promotable(state, 3, 3).
    For each promotable: add to accounts list as tier='tracked', topics inferred from recent tweet text, added=today.
    Accounts in state with appearances==1 and total_likes==0 → acct_state.mark_noise(state, author_id).
    New-voice cashtag tweets (author NOT in accounts.json before this run) → include in pool with tier='new'.
    Save state. Save accounts.json if any promotions.

  STEP 3 — Score + filter:
    Combined pool = timeline tweets + new-voice search tweets.
    Deduplicate by tweet ID using load_seen/save_seen.
    Skip is_spam.
    Score with engagement_score.
    ZEN bucket: text contains ZEN or $ZEN or Horizen (case-insensitive).
    VFY bucket: text contains VFY or $VFY or zkVerify or zkverify (case-insensitive).
    Tweet can appear in both. Sort each bucket by score desc, take top 8.

  STEP 4 — Sentiment per bucket (carry from v1).

  STEP 5 — Build + send email:
    Subject: f'$ZEN / $VFY X Monitor — {date} ({total_tracked} accounts tracked)'
    total_tracked = count of accounts in accounts.json with tier in (seed, tracked), or 0 if no file.
    new_promoted = count promoted this run.
    HTML: header with date + total_tracked + new_promoted. ZEN section (badge map: seed→🌱, tracked→✅, new→🆕). VFY section. Footer.
    --dry-run: print subject + plain text, do not call gog, exit 0.

Python 3.9 compatible, stdlib only.

userStories.title: Deploy scripts to Jack's machine via SCP
userStories.description:
Current state: All three scripts have been written and tested on Jill's workspace at businesses/horizen-zkverify/scripts/. Jack's machine (10.120.60.218) currently has only zen_vfy_monitor.py (v1) and .zen_vfy_seen.json.

What to build: A deploy step using run_command to SCP the three new files to Jack.

Commands to run (in order):

  2. scp businesses/horizen-zkverify/scripts/accounts_state.py jack@10.120.60.218:/Users/jack/.openclaw/workspace/businesses/horizen-zkverify/scripts/accounts_state.py

Note: SCP uses key-based auth (no password). Run from workspace root. The existing .zen_vfy_seen.json on Jack must NOT be overwritten.
